subject: Distance model chi-square GOF and bootstrap error

messages.author: d4a835914e61fc5b
messages.subject: Distance model chi-square GOF and bootstrap error
parts:
Hello all,

I am running chi-square GOF tests and parametric bootstraps on
distance sampling models for multiple species. All species' chi-
square GOF and bootstrap ran fine except for one, and I got this
error:

Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, …) : non-
finite finite-difference value [4]

Any ideas? The chi-square GOF and bootstrap code is the same as the
other species', save the top model inserted in the bootstrap
statement.

Any help would be greatly appreciated,

Sarah

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Distance model chi-square GOF and bootstrap error
parts:
Hi Sarah,

Can you post the fitted model output? And have you tried re-running parboot()? For some reason the model can't fit at least one of the simulated datasets, but it's hard to say why without more information. If you repeatedly issue the command:

simulate(fm)

where "fm" is your fitted model, do the simulated data look reasonable to you? Are they somewhat consistent with the observed data? Are any of the parameter estimates near a boundary? Did you standardize your covariates?

Richard

_____________________________________
Richard Chandler, post-doc
USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Distance model chi-square GOF and bootstrap error
parts:
hi Auriel,
 I would try to modify the function that you're bootstrapping to use the data-generating values as the starting values and see if that improves things.
 Possibly also there is just a problem here with too many parameters and, in particular, phi close to 1 for some simulated data set. It might be possibly to trap these failed cases out using some fancy R programming ... somehow.... but I don't have any great ideas. There is an R function "trycatch" which I've seen people use for trapping errors.  You might look into it....

regards
andy

parts:
Hi Auriel,

Along Andy's idea of using 'trycatch' or 'try':
I had a quick look at the unmarked source code and in case you use function parboot it would be straight forward to use 'try'.
The function does this:

        fits[[i]] <- update(object, data=simdata, starts=ests, se=FALSE)

if you adjust this slightly to something like this:
           
         #before "for(i in 1:nsim)" loop
         index <- 1  

        class(dummy <- try(update(object, data=simdata, starts=ests, se=FALSE))) == "unmarkedFitOccu") {
            fits[[index]] <- dummy
            index <- index + 1
        }

you should be able to have bootstrap continue running after an iteration does not work i.e. produce an error. If that's a good idea is a different question, but it could work.
One thing about the snippet above: "unmarkedFitOccu" needs to be replaced with whatever class our models actually have.
If you need help implementing this let me know and I can test this for you.

Cheers,
Richard S

On Tuesday, November 10, 2015 at 7:19:19 AM UTC-6, Richard Schuster wrote:
Hi Auriel,

Along Andy's idea of using 'trycatch' or 'try':
I had a quick look at the unmarked source code and in case you use function parboot it would be straight forward to use 'try'.
The function does this:

        fits[[i]] <- update(object, data=simdata, starts=ests, se=FALSE)

if you adjust this slightly to something like this:
           
         #before "for(i in 1:nsim)" loop
         index <- 1  

        class(dummy <- try(update(object, data=simdata, starts=ests, se=FALSE))) == "unmarkedFitOccu") {
            fits[[index]] <- dummy
            index <- index + 1
        }

you should be able to have bootstrap continue running after an iteration does not work i.e. produce an error. If that's a good idea is a different question, but it could work.
One thing about the snippet above: "unmarkedFitOccu" needs to be replaced with whatever class our models actually have.
If you need help implementing this let me know and I can test this for you.

Cheers,
Richard S

hi Auriel,
 I would try to modify the function that you're bootstrapping to use the data-generating values as the starting values and see if that improves things.
 Possibly also there is just a problem here with too many parameters and, in particular, phi close to 1 for some simulated data set. It might be possibly to trap these failed cases out using some fancy R programming ... somehow.... but I don't have any great ideas. There is an R function "trycatch" which I've seen people use for trapping errors.  You might look into it....

regards
andy

      if (class(fmP) == "try-error") {v<-1} else {

On Tuesday, November 10, 2015 at 7:19:19 AM UTC-6, Richard Schuster wrote:
Hi Auriel,

Along Andy's idea of using 'trycatch' or 'try':
I had a quick look at the unmarked source code and in case you use function parboot it would be straight forward to use 'try'.
The function does this:

        fits[[i]] <- update(object, data=simdata, starts=ests, se=FALSE)

if you adjust this slightly to something like this:
           
         #before "for(i in 1:nsim)" loop
         index <- 1  

        class(dummy <- try(update(object, data=simdata, starts=ests, se=FALSE))) == "unmarkedFitOccu") {
            fits[[index]] <- dummy
            index <- index + 1
        }

you should be able to have bootstrap continue running after an iteration does not work i.e. produce an error. If that's a good idea is a different question, but it could work.
One thing about the snippet above: "unmarkedFitOccu" needs to be replaced with whatever class our models actually have.
If you need help implementing this let me know and I can test this for you.

Cheers,
Richard S

I've tried both the methods propose by Marc and Richard. With Richard's suggestion I got the same output: stopped after a few simulations. With Richard's I´ve went a little bit farther, but can not achieve the update. I am coping here "my" updated version following the instructions, to see if anybody can give me an idea about what I am doing wrong.

Thanks a lot anyway.
Juan




updated.gof <- function (object, statistic = SSE, nsim = 10, report, 
                      ...) 
  {
    statistic <- match.fun(statistic)
    call <- match.call(call = sys.call(-1))
    formula <- object@formula
    umf <- getData(object)
    y <- getY(umf)
    if (class(object) %in% c("unmarkedFitOccu", "unmarkedFitOccuRN", 
                             "unmarkedFitGDS")) 
      y <- truncateToBinary(y)
    ests <- as.numeric(coef(object))
    t0 <- statistic(object, ...)
    lt0 <- length(t0)
    t.star <- matrix(NA, nsim, lt0)
    if (!is.null(names(t0))) 
      colnames(t.star) <- names(t0)
    else colnames(t.star) <- paste("t*", 1:lt0, sep = "")
    if (!missing(report)) 
      cat("t0 =", t0, "\n")
    fits <- list()
    simdata <- umf
    simList <- simulate(object, nsim = nsim, na.rm = FALSE)
 
   index <- 1
    
    for (i in 1:nsim) {
      y.sim <- simList[[i]]
      is.na(y.sim) <- is.na(y)
      simdata@y <- y.sim
     
      class(dummy <- try(update(object, data=simdata, starts=ests, se=FALSE)) == "unmarkedFitGDS")

fits[[index]] <- dummy
        index <- index + 1

t.star[i, ] <- statistic(fits[[i]], ...)
      if (!missing(report)) {
        if (nsim > report && i %in% seq(report, nsim, 
                                        by = report)) 
          cat(paste(round(t.star[(i - (report - 1)):i, 
                                 ], 1), collapse = ","), fill = TRUE)
      }
    }
    out <- new("parboot", call = call, t0 = t0, t.star = t.star)
    return(out)

}
